desc:
Cart and checkout product recommendations put a small, useful add on in front of shoppers at the moment they are ready to buy. Ecom Swift LLC builds the cart block, sets the rules and tests every discount and shipping path.

## Why the cart is the right place for suggestions

The cart is the one page where every shopper has already decided to buy something. A relevant add on here feels like a helpful reminder, such as a charger beside a phone case or a care kit beside a leather bag. The same suggestion on a busy home page would be easy to ignore.

Done badly, the cart is also the worst place for clutter. A large block of unrelated products pulls attention away from the checkout button and can lead shoppers to leave. The aim is a short, quiet block that adds value without getting in the way.

## What are cart add on recommendations?

Cart add on recommendations are suggested products shown in the cart page or cart drawer, based on what the shopper has already added. They are usually accessories, refills, matching items or a small gift. Each one shows a clear price and can be added with one tap.

## How cart suggestions affect orders

Suggestions in the cart can raise the value of each order when the extra item is something the shopper genuinely needs. The mechanism is low effort: the shopper does not search, open a new page or lose their place. They add the item and carry on to checkout.

A free shipping hint works in a similar way. When a shopper sees how close they are to the threshold, a small add on becomes a sensible choice rather than an upsell. The effect depends on your prices, your products and how relevant the suggestions are, so we treat it as something to measure and adjust.

## What a strong cart block includes

- Up to a few suggestions, never a long wall of products.
- Clear prices and a single tap to add.
- Rules based on what is in the cart, not random best sellers.
- Items already in the cart hidden from the list.
- A free shipping progress hint where it fits your store.
- Layouts that work in both the cart page and the cart drawer.
- Variant handling, so a shopper never adds the wrong size by accident.
- Rules that skip low stock items or low margin items.
- Easy removal of any item, so shoppers can always continue.

## How we build it

We begin by reviewing your cart page or drawer and your best selling combinations. We agree which items belong beside which, then set the rules by cart contents or, in the Premium package, by your order data. We style the block to match your theme.

Then we test every path we can think of: discount codes, automatic discounts, shipping thresholds, gift cards, express payment buttons and an empty cart. We check the layout on small phones, where space is tight. Standard adds rules by cart contents and a mobile check. Premium adds order based suggestions, an optional upsell on the checkout page, click tracking and a period of adjustments after launch.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Suggest items that clearly belong with what is in the cart.
- Keep the block short and the add button obvious.
- Show the price next to every suggestion.
- Test with discounts and shipping rules switched on.
- Review which add ons get clicked and adjust the rules.

**Avoid:**
- Adding items that cost more than the main purchase.
- Showing products that are out of stock.
- Pushing the checkout button below the fold on mobile.
- Using pop ups that block the cart.
- Suggesting something the shopper has already added.

## Who this is for

This service suits stores with natural accessories or refills, such as phone cases, skin care, pet supplies or coffee. It also suits stores whose average order is just under their free shipping line. A store with very few products may prefer a simple gift or sample offer, which we can handle as an add on.

## What we need from you

Send us a short list of products that go well together and any items you never want suggested. Tell us about your shipping thresholds and discount setup. We need collaborator, staff or developer access to your store, and we never ask for passwords. You review the block on a preview before it goes live.
